2608.25152.title: Belief Cascades Drive Persuasion in LLM Agent Networks
2608.25152.paper_summary: Multi-agent LLM systems increasingly debate answers, coordinate research, simulate users, and mediate information flows, making agent-to-agent persuasion a basic but undermeasured capability. We introduce a controlled testbed for studying how goal-directed persuaders shift elicited stances in networks of LLM agents grounded in real-world ego-network topologies. Across four LLM backbones, five graphs, and 55 policy statements, we find that persuasion dynamics depend on the interaction between topology, competition, topic, and model prior. Additionally, we show that direct exposure reliably predicts next-round stance change in competing runs, and peer relays carry smaller but measurable influence, showing that agents not assigned to persuade can still transmit persuasive force. Finally, analyzing post text alone misses important movement: planned strategies are only partly realized in executed messages, action choices can diverge from message content, and persuadees rarely state the stance shifts detected by probes. These results argue for evaluating multi-agent persuasion as a trajectory- and exposure-level process, using belief probes, exposure provenance, and action logs to identify who influenced whom and whether visible language reflects underlying stance movement.
2608.25152.paper_summary_zh: 多智能體 LLM 系統越來越多地辯論答案、協調研究、模擬用戶並調解信息流，這使得智能體之間的說服成為一種基本但未被充分測量的能力。我們引入了一個受控測試平台，用於研究以現實世界自我網絡拓撲為基礎的 LLM 智能體網絡中，目標導向的說服者如何改變引發的立場。在四個 LLM 主幹、五個圖形和 55 條政策聲明中，我們發現說服動態取決於拓撲、競爭、主題和模型先驗之間的相互作用。此外，我們顯示直接曝光可靠地預測競爭運行中的下一輪立場變化，而同儕中繼則帶來較小但可測量的影響，顯示未被指派說服的智能體仍然可以傳遞說服力。最後，僅分析後文會錯過重要的變化：計劃的策略在執行的消息中僅部分實現，行動選擇可能與消息內容有所偏離，而被說服者很少表明探測到的立場變化。這些結果主張將多智能體說服評估為一個軌跡和曝光層級的過程，使用信念探針、曝光來源和行動日誌來識別誰影響了誰，以及可見的語言是否反映了潛在的立場變化。
